To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Ntr phosphotransfer system (PTS) regulates the K+ uptake system Kdp in E. coli.

the Ntr phosphotransfer system controls K+ homeostases by regulating the expression of the K+ uptake system Kdp and that the Ntr system is also involved in the cross talk between K+ and carbohydrate metabolism.
the Ntr–PTS regulates the high‐affinitiy K+ transporter KDPFABC by stimulating the activity of the K+ sensor kinase KDPD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the high‐K+ uptake system KdpFABC.
the regulation of K+ homeostases in E.coli
the question of how the K+ homeostatic system of Escherichia coli is regulated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IIANtr, the Ntr‐PST and KdpFABC are part of a regulatory network that senses and responds to K+ and carbon source availability.

the Ntr–IIANtr system is a sensor of the intracellular K+ status, and the Ntr–Kdp system is a sensor for the intracellular K+/glucose ratio, and both systems are involved in the regulation of K+ homeostase in Escherichichia coli.
the Ntr–PTS regulates kdpFABC gene expression via the KdpD/KDP‐E two‐component system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ntr system is a sensor for the K+ and carbon status of the cell.

KdpD, a sensor kinase of the two‐component signal transduction system KdpD/E, is regulated by the phosphotransferring protein IIANtr of the phosphoenol pyruvate‐dependent phosphotransfer system Ntr‐PTS.
the Ntr system senses and integrates the nutritional status and the availability of K+ in order to control the expression of KdpFABC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ntr–PTS is an important regulatory system in the control of K+ uptake and homeostasis.
the Ntr–phosphoenolpyruate phosphotranserase system (Ntr–PTS) regulates the activity of the K+ sensor KdpD by direct interaction.
the Ntr-PTS, a parallel phosphoryl group transfer system, has an important role maintaining K+ homeo-stasis.
